results.name: Straight Bar Cable Pull Down
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attached to the high pulley. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, palms facing down.

Slightly bend your knees, push your hips back, and lean your torso forward slightly. Pull the bar down towards your thighs in a straight line, keeping your arms straight and your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the bar down until it reaches your thighs, feeling a strong contraction in your lats.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in your lats. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Adjust the weight on the cable machine to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Straight Bar Cable Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Straight Bar Cable Row Close Grip
instructions: Sit at a cable row machine with your feet placed on the footrests and knees slightly bent. Grasp the straight bar with a close grip, palms facing down.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back. Pull the bar towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold the contraction for a moment, feeling the muscles in your back activating.
Slowly extend your arms to return the bar to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the bar towards you and inhale as you extend your arms.
Adjust the weight on the cable machine to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Straight Bar Cable Row Close Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Superman Pulls Resistance Bands
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended straight out in front of you and your legs extended straight behind you.
Simultaneously lift your arms and chest off the floor as high as you comfortably can, engaging your lower back and glutes.
While holding the lifted position, bend your elbows and pull your arms back towards your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Extend your arms back out in front of you and slowly lower your chest back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift and pull the resistance band, and inhale as you extend your arms and lower your body.
Gradually increase the duration of the hold and the number of repetitions as your strength improves.
Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
results.description: Superman Pulls Resistance Bands is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Superman Pulls
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with a resistance band secured to a low anchor point in front of you. Hold one end of the resistance band in each hand with your arms extended straight out in front of you and your legs extended straight behind you.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor as high as you comfortably can, engaging your lower back and glutes.
While holding the lifted position, bend your elbows and pull the resistance band towards your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.

Extend your arms back out in front of you, keeping tension on the resistance band, and then slowly lower your arms, chest, and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your lower back and glute muscles to lift your body off the floor.
Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Use a mat to provide cushioning and support for your body.
results.description: Superman Pulls is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Supine Push Up
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Position your elbows to your sides with your forearms perpendicular to the floor and hands kept closed.
Engage your core and press your elbows into the floor, lifting your upper back and shoulders off the floor.
Hold the lifted position for a second, feeling the contraction in your upper back.
Slowly lower your upper back and shoulders back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift your upper back and shoulders, and inhale as you lower them back down.
Focus on using your shoulders and upper back muscles to lift your upper body off the floor.
Use a mat to provide cushioning and support for your back.
results.description: Supine Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Bent Knee Inverted Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lean back, extend your arms, and lift your hips off the floor, keeping your body in a straight line from head to knees parallel to the floor.
Pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your back muscles to pull yourself up, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Bent Knee Inverted Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chin-Up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to an overhead position. Stand directly beneath the handles and grasp them with an underhand grip (palms facing you), shoulder-width apart.
Pull your body up towards the handles by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles, focusing on engaging your biceps and back muscles.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your body up and inhale as you lower back down.
Adjust the height of the suspension trainer straps to ensure a full range of motion.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chin-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips High Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lean back, extending your arms fully while keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your core tight to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Adjust the length of the suspension trainer straps to increase or decrease the difficulty of the exercise.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you extend your arms back.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips High Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps, Forearms.
